subject: ventures/gift-vs-inherit-basis-calculator
professional: an estate-planning CPA or attorney who advises on gift versus bequest basis

evidence.correctness: Ran node against calc.mjs and recomputed by hand from IRC 1014/1015, 121, 2001/2010, 2503(b), Treas. Reg. 1.1015-1(a)(2) and 2026 figures (15,000,000 exemption, 19,000 exclusion; recalled from the statutes and Rev. Proc., not fetched). Default gift tax 119,788.25, sell-now 20,900, large-estate inherit and gift estate tax (9,433,496.58 and 6,792,400), taxable gift and 709 boundary all match to the cent. One departure: giftGain(50000,90000,450000) returns -400,000, expected -40,000 (latent, losses are not used downstream). Gift-tax basis adjustment missing.
evidence.completeness: Every claimed feature works end to end: three-path table, 709 flag, five-horizon sensitivity, CSV (4 rows), editable exemption and exclusion, disclaimer, not-decided list. Page inputs are filled by JS; blank fields fall back to defaults silently. No TODOs or dead links in the venture; related-tool links point at sibling ventures.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' gives 23 pass, 0 fail. Six seeded mutations, four survived (709 boundary, NIIT, sell-now estate base, priorGifts in inheritance); two were caught (loss branch, annual exclusion). All files restored with git checkout, git status clean. Tests assert values the author computed; none covers the rule branch that is wrong.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (129 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script. Small pure functions, escaped HTML, no network, usage.mjs handles blocked storage. Defects: giftGain branch order, silent default on blank input (index.html:95), isHome as a 0/1 number field, no rate range validation.
evidence.claims: Loaded https://marisstella.app/gift-vs-inherit-basis-calculator/: llms.txt, sitemap and canonical carry marisstella.app, so the source-side github.io and ./ URLs are not defects. Disclaimer, privacy, sponsor link and usage events match code (page.test.mjs). README and page list what is not modelled. Overclaim: FAQ says the loss on a gifted loss property 'is not usable'. README and page omit the IRC 1015(d) adjustment.
evidence.fitness: A homeowner or adult child can enter value, basis, years and see a dollar figure per path and a 709 flag, which is the job. Gaps: user must know their own federal rate and NIIT, blank fields are replaced silently, the sell-now column is not horizon-matched, and TOD deed or revocable trust (the page's own recommended alternatives) are not priced.
evidence.domain: Professional: an estate-planning attorney or CPA doing basis planning. They would accept carryover vs step-up, dual-basis intent, and unified-credit arithmetic as a first screen. They would check first the loss-property rule (departure above), 1015(d), 121 loss on the donee side, the 1014(e) one-year rule, and that the comparison omits growth on sold cash. Flat 40% above exemption is correct for estates over the 15M exemption.

mutations.change: loss branch: price - valueAtGift -> price - basis
sell-now estate base: v - nowTax -> v

defects.what: giftGain applies the fair-value loss rule to every sale below fair value at gift, even when donor basis is below fair value; sale of 90,000-basis, 450,000-FMV property at 50,000 returns -400,000, not -40,000. Latent today because gainTax ignores losses and the UI does not show gift.gain, but it is exported and wrong; tests only cover basis above FMV.
Survivors: NIIT rate, sell-now estate base, priorGifts in inheritance, and the 709 boundary have no test; a change to any leaves 23 tests green.
A blank or cleared input silently becomes the example default (e.g. blank basis becomes 90,000) and the result is shown with no warning.
FAQ says a loss on gifted loss property is not usable; IRC 1015(a) lets the recipient claim the loss measured from fair value at gift. The tool also never credits such a loss.
Gift-tax basis adjustment (IRC 1015(d)) is neither modelled nor listed under not modelled.

Sell-now path has no growth on the cash and is compared with paths at the death horizon, so 'Lowest tax' mixes horizons; rates (15/20, NIIT) are typed by the user with no bracket help; growth below -100 is not rejected.

verdict: Arithmetic is right: the default and large-estate cases, the 709 test and the exemption maths reproduce by hand to the cent, the served page and llms.txt are correct after the deploy rewrite, and every advertised feature works. It does not meet the bar because verification is 2: four of six seeded mutations survived, including NIIT and the 709 boundary. A professional would also find giftGain wrong for appreciated property sold below donor basis (latent), a FAQ line that misstates the loss rule, silent defaults for blank inputs and no 1015(d) adjustment. Fine as a first screen with a stated-limits disclaimer, not as a planning tool.
